which lends to human society its salutary order and dignity.
And he comes to experience the joy that is granted him when
he uses the power of thought and insight not only in the
service of the practical ends of life, but also and above all
when he uses and trains them to grasp the truth, to under-
stand the world as it really is and himself as he really is. He
learns to know the joy of brightening the prosaic hues of
everyday life with the radiance of artistic achievements, of
decorating life with the garlands of the beautiful.
But man lives at the same time in the visible world which is
ruled by sheer hunger and brutal power. Nature seems to
conspire against the world of the spirit. Material needs,
want and sickness, rob the spirit of its freedom and subdue
it to the world of the physical. The question as to what
is good is superseded by the question as to what is useful.
The understanding of truth and knowledge is exploited
by the technology of practical life aims. The hours of up-
lifting joy in the contemplation of beauty grow few, and art
no longer serves the delight and strengthening of the spirit
but is prostituted in the service of entertainment and dis-
traction. And we must go further and say that human society
itself seems to be hostile to the life of the spirit. Right cannot
be maintained without power, and how often does power
come before right! How much better fare those people who
are concerned with questions of the profitable rather than
the good! So often does the lie triumph over truth, ambition
over the tranquil surrender to the recognition of what is
true and the ideal of beauty.
. Thus man is constantly pressed by the temptation to
abandon that life in two worlds which so often tears his
breast and instead to follow purely practical life aims. He is
faced by the decision: is he to yield to the absolute obliga-
tions with which the world of the spirit confronts him and
in its service to shoulder a double burden of torment and
trial? Is he to preserve the faith that he lives his true essen-
tial life only in the world of the spirit? At all times there
